note: Python FastAPI plus OpenAI Agents SDK. The browser only calls the app's own backend, so no ai_browser_call. No login on any endpoint. .env.example and k8s/secret.yml were blocked, so secret_exposure is not covered.

labels.what: Prompt says never resolve a ticket when latest sentiment is below 0.3 (also lines 39-41). update_ticket only checks the status transition and never looks at sentiment
Prompt says always add resolution notes when resolving. The tool takes resolution_notes as optional and accepts status resolved with none
Prompt says MUST escalate and NOT answer for refunds, billing disputes, legal, account deletion and low sentiment. send_response has no check, so the model can still send an answer
Never discuss competitor products: no output filter in send_response, only the prompt
send_response writes the outbound reply to the customer straight from the model text with no approval step. Only a length cut to channel max_length is applied
update_ticket lets the model mark a ticket resolved with no human check
create_ticket inserts channel, category and priority exactly as the model passes them, no allowlist in code (it only checks the customer exists). No cap on tickets per customer or per run
send_response creates a ticket itself as a fallback and accepts any conversation_id and channel from the model with no check that they belong to the same customer
escalate_to_human sets status escalated on any ticket id with no status or ownership check; escalated is a terminal state
send_response only stores the message in the database. For gmail and whatsapp delivered is false and nothing is sent (comment says deferred). Only web works
The tool logs 'Response sent' for gmail and whatsapp though nothing was delivered. The model still tells the customer help is on the way
15+ sample help articles for a generic 'our platform' SaaS using app.example.com. Seed content for the knowledge base; the agent answers from it as if real company docs
GET /api/tickets/{ticket_id} and GET /api/customers/{customer_id}/history have no login. Anyone with a UUID reads ticket messages and customer history
GET /api/jobs/{job_id} has no login or owner check; anyone with a job id reads another customer's agent reply
Gmail and WhatsApp webhook endpoints accept any POST with no signature or secret check, so anyone can inject a customer identity and message
POST /api/chat starts a paid model run per request with no rate limit or auth. email is a free string, not validated
Customer email and message are joined into the model prompt with an f-string with no guard. The agent then trusts the email as identity (also line 136, 285, 303)
Cross-channel linking attaches a new phone or email to an existing customer by asking the user for an email. No proof of ownership, so a caller can link to and read another person's history
CORS allows all origins with allow_credentials true
Global error handler returns str(exc) to the client, leaking internal error text
API URL falls back to http://localhost:8000 in browser code
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL set to http://localhost:8000 as a build arg
Per-channel max_length 1500/2500/800 seeded in the migration. The prompt gives style per channel but no length, so the limits live in one place only
POSTGRES_PASSWORD defaults to 'postgres' when the env var is unset (also line 77 in DATABASE_URL)
Plain Postgres schema (customers, tickets, messages, knowledge_base, metrics) with no row-level security or roles; backend connects as postgres user. Not exposed to browser, so low risk
